title: What If Sirius Replaced Our Sun?

scenes.text: What if Sirius replaced our Sun? The bright star would be a death sentence, not a gift.
Sirius A is about twenty-five times more luminous than the Sun, and twice as massive.
Earth would get roughly twenty-five times today's sunlight. Oceans would heat up far past anything we have seen.
The sky would turn a harsh blue-white, because Sirius burns at nearly ten thousand Kelvin.
Ice caps, forests and cities would not survive. Earth would lose its water to space.
And Sirius would burn out far faster. Its core hydrogen runs low within about a billion years.
